title: eval-harness: add CI gating for prompt-set regressions and quality metric integrations
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We need reliable automatic detection of prompt-set regressions and quality drops in model-facing changes. This PR introduces CI gating hooks into the eval-harness pipeline that run a small, focused prompt-set and a set of thresholded metrics (accuracy/rouge/semantic-similarity) on staged model variants. The goal is to block merges that introduce statistically significant regressions against a baseline proto-eval. What this changes: - New CI job definitions (circleci & GitHub Actions) that can be enabled per-repo. Jobs run the eval-harness runner in a lightweight mode and publish a pass/fail artifact. - Evaluation config: added eval/configs/ci_prompt_sets.yaml and threshold profiles in eval/configs/ci_thresholds.yaml. These are intentionally conservative to avoid noisy failures; thresholds are configurable in repo-specific overrides. - Metric integrations: wire up existing rouge and embedding-sim similarity checks, plus a new fast approximate confidence-regression detector. Results are summarized in a single JSON artifact that the CI step uploads. - Gating logic: a small Python utility (eval/tools/ci_gate.py) that reads the artifact and returns non-zero when any configured metric crosses its thresholds. This utility supports guarding by sample size and p-value (simple bootstrap test). - Local runner: a new dev script (scripts/eval_ci_local.sh) to run the same checks locally for developers. Testing and rollout: - Unit tests for ci_gate and config parsing added (tests/eval/test_ci_gate.py). - Integration tests run in CI; flakiness observed initially on embedding-sim in open-source model runs. We mitigated by reducing sample size variance and adding a retry wrapper in the CI job. - Rollout plan: feature is behind a repo-level flag (eval.ci_gating.enabled) and disabled by default for non-redwood repos. We will enable for core eval-harness and redwood repo after one week of monitor-only runs. Related tickets: ENG-2142 (eval gating PoC), ENG-2178 (threshold profiles), SUP-8421 (customer-reported regression that motivated better CI). Checklist: - [x] Add CI job definitions and gating utility - [x] Add conservative threshold profiles - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Add developer local runner - [x] Update README / docs with gating instructions Notes: This is intentionally conservative; thresholds can be tuned as we gain signal. We recommend enabling monitor-only mode for the first week to collect baselines.

review_comments:

release_notes: Add a conservative CI gate for eval-harness that runs a small prompt-set and thresholded metrics to detect regressions early. Includes config for thresholds, gating utility, CI job definitions, local dev runner, and docs.
notes_for_ops: If enabling in monitor-only mode, configure eval.ci_gating.mode=monitor in repo config. To fully enforce gating, set mode=block and ensure baseline artifacts are available at eval/ci/baselines/<repo>.json. Monitor job outputs to tune thresholds the first week.
testing_instructions: Run scripts/eval_ci_local.sh to simulate CI gating locally; CI jobs are defined under .github/workflows/eval-harness-gate.yaml and circleci config. See docs/eval/ci_gating.md for examples and override options.
